raw_case_text:
A 76-year-old female presented with painful swelling in the left lateral neck region for 15 days. There was no erythema or heating sensation on neck area, and she had no symptoms of fever. Ten months earlier, she had undergone total thyroidectomy with central neck lymph node dissection due to PTC (T3N1aM0 by American Joint Committee on Cancer/International Union against Cancer Staging System 7th Edition), followed by radioactive iodine therapy and maintenance treatment with levothyroxine.
Thyroid function tests showed mildly suppressed thyrotropin-stimulating hormone (TSH; 0.01 mIU/L; normal range, 0.27-4.2 mIU/L) and elevated free thyroxine (fT4; 2.12 ng/dL; normal range, 0.93-1.70 ng/dL) concentrations. Her white blood cell and neutrophil counts were normal. No pathogens were cultured from her blood, stool, urine, or sputum.
Neck ultrasonography revealed a large heterogeneous echoic (cystic) mass in the left lateral neck (Figure 1) and computed tomography revealed a 3.3 x 5.6 cm sized thick-walled cystic lesion along left levels II, III, and IV (Figure 2). Cytologic examination of the dark brown colored fluid collected from the lesion by fine-needle aspiration showed many neutrophils and macrophages in necrotic background, but there was no evidence of malignancy (Figure 3). However, the mass was suspected of being a metastatic lymph node and was resected.
Intraoperative examination showed that mass was encapsulated and very highly adhesive to the internal jugular vein and around the tissue. There were no other abnormally enlarged lymph nodes. The mass contained dark brown colored fluid and some debris. Microscopic examination of the lymph node mass showed massive necrosis and immunohistochemistry clearly showed that the mass was a metastatic papillary carcinoma (Figure 4). Culture of the fluid showed the presence of Salmonella Typhi.
No postoperative complications occurred. The patient was treated with intravenous cephalosporin for 6 days; following antibiotic sensitivity testing of the cultured Salmonella Typhi, she was switched to oral ciprofloxacin for 7 days. Regular follow-up examinations have shown no evidence of additional metastasis, recurrence of metastasis, or residual infection.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 76-year-old female presented with painful swelling in the left lateral neck for 15 days.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed a painful swelling in the left lateral neck region of 15 days' duration. There was no local erythema, warmth, or fever. Ten months prior to presentation, she underwent total thyroidectomy with central neck lymph node dissection for papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC, stage T3N1aM0), followed by radioactive iodine therapy and maintenance levothyroxine therapy.
subjective.past_medical_history: Papillary thyroid carcinoma (AJCC/UICC 7th edition stage T3N1aM0) treated 10 months prior with total thyroidectomy and central neck dissection, followed by radioactive iodine ablation and maintenance levothyroxine suppression therapy.
subjective.review_of_systems: Painful lateral neck swelling. Denies fever, chills, local erythema, warmth, or gastrointestinal complaints.

objective.physical_examination: Painful swelling/mass in the left lateral neck without erythema or increased local temperature. Afebrile.
objective.routine_investigations: White blood cell and neutrophil counts were normal. TSH was mildly suppressed at 0.01 mIU/L (normal range 0.27-4.2 mIU/L), and free T4 was elevated at 2.12 ng/dL (normal range 0.93-1.70 ng/dL). Blood, stool, urine, and sputum cultures were negative for pathogens.
objective.advanced_workup: Neck ultrasonography showed a large heterogeneous echoic (cystic) mass in the left lateral neck. Contrast-enhanced neck CT revealed a 3.3 x 5.6 cm thick-walled cystic lesion along left cervical levels II, III, and IV. Fine-needle aspiration (FNA) yielded dark brown fluid; cytological examination demonstrated abundant neutrophils and macrophages in a necrotic background without malignant cells. Surgical excision revealed an encapsulated mass densely adherent to the internal jugular vein and adjacent tissues containing necrotic debris and dark brown fluid; histopathological and immunohistochemical examination confirmed metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma with massive necrosis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi abscess / bacterial infection localized within a necrotic metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma cervical lymph node. Fluid culture from the resected mass yielded Salmonella Typhi. Blood, stool, sputum, and urine cultures were all sterile.
Plan & Outcome: Complete surgical excision of the infected metastatic nodal mass without postoperative complications. Treated with intravenous cephalosporin for 6 days, then transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin for 7 days based on antibiotic susceptibility testing of the S. Typhi isolate. Regular follow-up examinations showed no evidence of residual infection, local recurrence, or distant metastases.
